questions.question_text: Hadith 3 of An-Nawawi's collection states, 'Actions are according to their intentions.' What is the primary lesson derived from this Hadith?

options.text: The importance of performing actions with sincerity
The reward for good deeds is doubled
The necessity of following the Sunnah in all actions
The prohibition of certain actions without proper intention

questions.explanation: The primary lesson derived from Hadith 3 is the importance of performing actions with sincerity, as the reward or consequence of actions is determined by their intentions. This Hadith emphasizes the significance of having the right intention behind one's deeds.

questions.question_text: What is the primary characteristic that distinguishes a Sahih Hadith from other classifications?

options.text: It is narrated by a large number of companions
It has a continuous chain of reliable narrators
It is mentioned in the Qur'an
It is related to the life of the Prophet in Makkah

questions.explanation: A Sahih Hadith is considered authentic and is characterized by having a continuous chain of narrators who are known for their reliability and integrity. This ensures the Hadith is traceable back to the Prophet Muhammad without any breaks or weak links in the chain.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: During the revelation of the Qur'an, what was the primary method used by the Prophet Muhammad to preserve the revelations?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an was preserved through multiple methods during the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad. These included oral tradition among the companions, written records by the scribes appointed by the Prophet, and memorization by those known as Hafiz. Thus, all the mentioned methods were used.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in Allah's:

options.text: Lordship and control over all things

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah is the belief in Allah's lordship, acknowledging that He is the sole creator, owner, and controller of everything in the universe. This aspect of Tawhid emphasizes Allah's authority and dominion over all that exists.

The obligation of engaging in doubtful matters

questions.explanation: This Hadith teaches Muslims to be cautious and avoid doubtful matters, as they may lead to unlawful actions. The Prophet (peace be upon him) advised believers to steer clear of such ambiguities to maintain their righteousness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a primary source of Shariah Law?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an is considered the primary source of Shariah Law, as it is the word of Allah as revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. The Sunnah is also a primary source, but among the given options, The Qur'an is the most direct answer.

questions.question_text: Hadith 4 of An-Nawawi's collection states, 'Verily Allah has prescribed proficiency in all things.' What is the primary lesson derived from this Hadith?

options.text: The importance of sincerity in actions
The necessity of perfection in every deed
The value of knowledge over action
The prohibition of innovation in religion

questions.explanation: The primary lesson derived from Hadith 4 is the importance of doing things with proficiency and excellence. It encourages Muslims to perform their tasks to the best of their ability, reflecting the Islamic value of striving for perfection in all aspects of life.

questions.question_text: Hadith 5 of An-Nawawi's collection states, 'The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, “We \(were\) on a journey with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) when a man came to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have lost my camel.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Go and find it.' The man searched and did not find it, then he came back and said, 'I have lost my camel.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Go and find it.' He searched again and did not find it, then he came back and said, 'I have lost my camel.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Go and find it. Tie it when you find it and take care of it, for Allah has commanded us to do so.' The man said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I am tired.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'You have tired yourself.' The man then found his camel.' What is the primary lesson derived from this Hadith?

options.text: The importance of perseverance in searching for something lost
The significance of praying for lost items
The need to rely solely on divine intervention
The value of seeking help from others in times of need

questions.explanation: The Hadith emphasizes the importance of taking action and being diligent in one's efforts. The Prophet (peace be upon him) instructs the man to continue searching for his camel, illustrating the value of perseverance. The correct answer, 'The importance of perseverance in searching for something lost,' reflects this lesson. The other options are incorrect because they either misinterpret the Hadith's message or introduce elements not present in the narrative.

This was done to standardize the text and prevent variations that had arisen due to the expansion of the Islamic state and the presence of different recitations. The other options are incorrect because while Abu Bakr initiated the collection of the Qur'an after the death of many memorizers in the Battle of Yamama, it was Uthman who standardized the text into a single, unified manuscript.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah is the belief in Allah's sole lordship over the universe. Which of the following is a manifestation of this belief?

options.text: Belief in the oneness of Allah in worship
Acknowledgment of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer
Adherence to the Five Pillars of Islam
Following the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in Allah's lordship, encompassing His role as the sole Creator, Owner, and Controller of the universe. The correct answer, 'Acknowledgment of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer,' accurately reflects this concept. The other options are incorrect because they either refer to different aspects of Tawhid (such as Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah in option A) or to practices and beliefs that, while important in Islam, do not directly manifest Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah.

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas primarily emphasizes the oneness of Allah (Tawhid), affirming that Allah is unique, eternal, and without associates or equals. It is a concise declaration of monotheism.

The narrator is known to be unreliable

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Falaq is about seeking refuge from evil, including the evil of darkness, the evil of witches, and the evil of the envier.

questions.question_text: The process of compiling the Qur'an into a single manuscript was initiated during the caliphate of which companion of the Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explanation: The compilation of the Qur'an into a single manuscript was initiated during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, but it was during the caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan that the standardization and distribution of the compiled Qur'an took place to ensure uniformity across the Islamic state. Thus, while Abu Bakr oversaw the initial compilation, Uthman ibn Affan is credited with the standardization.

The Hadith is widely known among scholars

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat refers to the belief in Allah's beautiful names and attributes as described in the Qur'an and Hadith. What is the primary principle guiding the understanding of these names and attributes?

options.text: Affirming the names and attributes as they are, without anthropomorphism or distortion
Rejecting any attributes not directly mentioned in the Qur'an

questions.explanation: The primary principle guiding the understanding of Allah's names and attributes is to affirm them as they are described in the Qur'an and Hadith, without anthropomorphism (Tashbih), distortion (Tahreef), or negation (Ta'teel). This approach ensures that the belief in Tawhid Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat is maintained in its pure form.

options.text: Guidance and prayer for the straight path

questions.question_text: Hadith 3 of An-Nawawi's collection states, 'Actions are according to their intentions.' What is the primary lesson derived from this Hadith?

options.text: The importance of sincerity in actions
The significance of rituals in Islam
The role of intentions in determining the value of deeds
The necessity of performing actions with haste

questions.explanation: This Hadith emphasizes that the value and acceptance of actions are determined by their underlying intentions. It teaches that actions are judged based on why they are performed, highlighting the importance of having the right intention. Thus, option C is correct as it directly reflects the primary lesson of the Hadith. Options A and B, while related to Islamic teachings, do not directly capture the essence of this specific Hadith. Option D is unrelated to the Hadith's message.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah refers to the belief in Allah's sole right to be worshipped. Which of the following is a manifestation of this belief?

options.text: Believing in the oneness of Allah's lordship
Directing all acts of worship to Allah alone
Acknowledging Allah's beautiful names and attributes
Following the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah is about dedicating all acts of worship exclusively to Allah, recognizing that He is the only deity worthy of worship. Thus, directing all acts of worship to Allah alone is a direct manifestation of this belief, making option B the correct answer. Option A refers to Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah, option C to Tawhid Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat, and option D, while important in Islam, is not a direct manifestation of Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah.

questions.question_text: What is the primary theme of Surah Al-Nas?

options.text: Seeking refuge from evil and mischief
The story of Prophet Muhammad's prophethood

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Nas is one of the Mu'awwidhatayn (the two surahs of seeking refuge) and is about seeking Allah's protection from the evil of the whisperer (Shaytan) who tries to mislead humans. Thus, the primary theme is seeking refuge from evil and mischief, making option A correct. Option B is the theme of Surah Al-Ikhlas, option C is a theme found in various surahs but not the primary theme of Al-Nas, and option D is not related to the content of Surah Al-Nas.

questions.question_text: According to Islamic law, what is the primary condition for the validity of a marriage contract (Nikah)?

options.text: Presence of the bride and groom
Presence of witnesses and the consent of the bride and groom
Payment of dowry (Mahr) by the groom
Conducting the ceremony in a mosque

questions.explanation: The primary condition for the validity of a Nikah includes the presence of witnesses and the consent of the bride and groom. This ensures the marriage is publicly acknowledged and agreed upon by both parties.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: What was the primary reason for compiling the Qur'an into a single manuscript during the caliphate of Abu Bakr?

options.text: To standardize the recitation and prevent variations
To translate the Qur'an into other languages
To create an illustrated version of the Qur'an
To use it as a historical document

questions.explanation: The primary reason for compiling the Qur'an into a single manuscript during the caliphate of Abu Bakr was to standardize the recitation and prevent variations. This was crucial as the Islamic community was expanding, and variations in recitation were emerging. By compiling the Qur'an into a single manuscript, the companions aimed to preserve the unity and accuracy of the text.

questions.question_text: What is the primary factor considered by scholars when evaluating the authenticity of a Hadith?

options.text: The historical context of the Hadith

questions.explanation: Scholars consider multiple factors when evaluating the authenticity of a Hadith, including the chain of narration (Sanad), the content of the Hadith (Matn), and the historical context. The chain of narration is crucial as it verifies the reliability of the reporters. The content is also examined for consistency with other authentic Hadiths and the Qur'an. The historical context helps in understanding the relevance and application of the Hadith.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat refers to the belief in Allah's beautiful names and attributes as described in the Qur'an and Hadith. Which of the following is a correct understanding of this concept?

options.text: Allah's attributes are to be interpreted literally without considering the context
Allah's attributes are to be understood metaphorically to avoid anthropomorphism
Allah's attributes are to be affirmed without likening Him to His creation
Allah's attributes are to be denied to avoid anthropomorphism

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat involves affirming Allah's beautiful names and attributes as described in the Qur'an and Hadith, without likening Him to His creation (Tashbih) or distorting their meaning (Ta'wil). This approach maintains the balance between affirming Allah's attributes and avoiding anthropomorphism.

questions.explanation: For a marriage contract (Nikah) to be valid according to Islamic law, several conditions must be met, including the presence of witnesses, the consent of the bride, and the payment of Mahr (dower). All these elements are crucial for the validity of the Nikah.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: The process of compiling the Qur'an into a single manuscript was initiated during the caliphate of which companion of the Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explanation: The compilation of the Qur'an into a single manuscript was initiated during the caliphate of Abu Bakr due to the need to preserve the Qur'an after many memorizers were killed in the Battle of Yamama. This was undertaken by Zayd ibn Thabit, who compiled the revelations into a single manuscript. Thus, the correct answer is Abu Bakr.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion used by scholars to classify a Hadith as Sahih (authentic)?

options.text: The chain of narration is unbroken and consists of trustworthy narrators
The Hadith is mentioned in a reputable Hadith collection
The Hadith is widely practiced by the Muslim community
The Hadith is in agreement with the Qur'an

questions.explanation: Scholars classify a Hadith as Sahih if its chain of narration is unbroken and consists of trustworthy narrators. This ensures the authenticity and reliability of the Hadith. Thus, the correct answer is 'The chain of narration is unbroken and consists of trustworthy narrators'.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat refers to the belief in Allah's beautiful names and attributes as described in the Qur'an and Hadith. Which of the following is a manifestation of this belief?

options.text: Believing in Allah's sole right to be worshipped
Understanding Allah's names and attributes as described in Islamic texts
Believing in the Day of Judgment

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat involves believing in and understanding Allah's names and attributes as described in the Qur'an and Hadith without distorting or denying them. Thus, the correct answer is 'Understanding Allah's names and attributes as described in Islamic texts'.

The value of brotherhood and mutual love in faith

questions.explanation: This Hadith emphasizes the importance of brotherhood and mutual love among Muslims, highlighting that true faith is not just about individual beliefs but also about how one treats others. questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in Allah's:
questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah is the belief in Allah's lordship over all creation, acknowledging that He is the sole Creator, Sustainer, and Controller of the universe. questions.question_text: What is the primary theme of Surah Al-Ikhlas?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas is a concise declaration of the oneness of Allah, emphasizing that He is unique and unparalleled. It is a fundamental statement of Tawhid, affirming that Allah is the One, the Eternal, and that He begets not nor was begotten.

questions.question_text: According to Hadith 9 of An-Nawawi's collection, what is the ruling on a person who innovates something new in Islam?

options.text: It is considered a good deed if the innovation is beneficial
It is considered a bad deed and is rejected
It is considered neutral and depends on the context
It is considered obligatory if it is related to worship

questions.explanation: Hadith 9 of An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes that any innovation in Islam that is not based on the Sunnah or the Qur'an is considered a bid'ah (innovation) and is rejected. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Every innovation is a going astray.' Therefore, the correct answer is B, as it aligns with the Prophetic saying that innovations not grounded in Islamic teachings are considered misguided.

questions.question_text: What is the concept of Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah?

options.text: The oneness of God in His Lordship
The oneness of God in worship
The oneness of God in His names and attributes
The unity of the Muslim community

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in the oneness of God in His Lordship, meaning that Allah is the sole Creator, Owner, and Controller of the universe. This concept is fundamental to Islamic theology and is acknowledged even by many non-Muslims. The correct answer is A, as it accurately describes Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah.

questions.question_text: Which Surah is known for its comprehensive summary of the Islamic faith and is recited in every unit of prayer?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fatihah is known as 'Umm Al-Qur'an' (the Mother of the Qur'an) because it provides a comprehensive summary of the Islamic faith. The prayer is valid as long as one has made an honest effort to face the Qiblah
The prayer must be repeated if the direction is later found to be incorrect
The prayer is always valid regardless of the direction faced

questions.explanation: According to Islamic jurisprudence, if a person performs Salat facing a direction other than the Qiblah due to genuine uncertainty or inability to determine the correct direction, their prayer is considered valid as long as they have made an honest effort to face the Qiblah. questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion used by scholars to classify a Hadith as 'Da'if'?

options.text: The chain of narration is uninterrupted
The narrator is known for honesty and accuracy
The Hadith contradicts a stronger Hadith
There is a break in the chain of narration or a narrator is unreliable

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as 'Da'if' (weak) if there is a break in the chain of narration or if one of the narrators is unreliable. This classification affects the Hadith's reliability and its use in legal or theological discussions.

questions.question_text: What does Tawhid Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat entail?

options.text: Belief in the oneness of God in His actions
Belief in the oneness of God in His names and attributes
Belief in the oneness of God in worship
Belief in the prophethood of Muhammad

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat refers to the belief in the oneness of God in His names and attributes. It involves affirming the names and attributes of God as described in the Qur'an and Hadith without distorting or denying them.

The distribution is based solely on the number of heirs

questions.question_text: What is the primary source of Shariah Law when dealing with matters not explicitly addressed in the Qur'an or Hadith?

Among these, Qiyas (Analogical Reasoning) is a primary method used to deduce rulings by comparing new issues to similar cases with known rulings in the Qur'an and Hadith. Thus, the correct answer is B.

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as 'Hasan' if its chain of narration is continuous and consists of trustworthy narrators, but one of the narrators has a slightly weaker memory. questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: What was the role of the companion Zayd ibn Thabit in the compilation of the Qur'an during the caliphate of Abu Bakr?

options.text: He was responsible for collecting the Qur'an from various sources and compiling it into a single manuscript.
He was the primary scribe of the Prophet Muhammad and played a key role in verifying the authenticity of the Qur'an.
He led the committee responsible for standardizing the Qur'anic manuscripts during the caliphate of Uthman.
He was tasked with memorizing the entire Qur'an and teaching it to others.

questions.explanation: During the caliphate of Abu Bakr, after the Battle of Yamama where many memorizers of the Qur'an were martyred, Zayd ibn Thabit was tasked with collecting the Qur'an from various sources such as parchments, stones, and the memories of the companions to compile it into a single manuscript. This was a crucial step in preserving the Qur'an.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion used by scholars to classify a Hadith as 'Hasan'?

options.text: The Hadith is narrated by a large number of companions.
The chain of narration is continuous and consists of narrators known for their integrity and strong memory.
The Hadith is found in the six canonical Hadith collections.
The chain of narration is continuous but one or more narrators have slightly weaker memory or integrity compared to those in 'Sahih' Hadith.

questions.explanation: A 'Hasan' Hadith is one where the chain of narration is continuous, but one or more narrators in the chain have slightly weaker memory or integrity compared to those found in 'Sahih' Hadith. However, the weakness is not significant enough to classify it as 'Da'if' (weak).

questions.question_text: Which aspect of Tawhid emphasizes the oneness of Allah in His Lordship, worship, and names and attributes?
questions.explanation: Tawhid is categorized into three main aspects: Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (oneness of Allah's Lordship), Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (oneness in worship), and Tawhid al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (oneness in Allah's names and attributes). Together, they encompass the comprehensive belief in the oneness of Allah.

questions.explanation: Surahs Al-Falaq and Al-Nas are collectively known as 'Al-Mu'awwidhatayn' (the two Surahs of seeking refuge). They are recited for protection against evil. Surah Al-Ikhlas, while not part of 'Al-Mu'awwidhatayn', is also significant in affirming the oneness of Allah.

questions.question_text: The first Hadith in An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes the importance of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The first Hadith in An-Nawawi's collection highlights the significance of intention (Niyyah) in actions, stating that actions are judged by their motives. This Hadith is fundamental in understanding the Islamic perspective on the importance of having the right intention behind one's deeds.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a category of Tawhid?
questions.explanation: Tawhid is categorized into three main types: Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (Oneness of Lordship), Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (Oneness of Worship), and Tawhid al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (Oneness of Allah's Names and Attributes). 'Tawhid al-Mutlaq' is not a recognized category within the traditional classification of Tawhid.

questions.question_text: Which Pillar of Islam is associated with the giving of a specific percentage of one's wealth to the needy?
questions.explanation: Zakat is the Pillar of Islam that involves giving a specific percentage (usually 2.5%) of one's wealth to the needy. It is a form of obligatory charity that purifies one's wealth and soul.

questions.question_text: The third Hadith in An-Nawawi's collection focuses on the concept of which Islamic principle?

options.text: Actions are judged by their intentions

questions.explanation: The third Hadith in An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes that 'Actions are judged by their intentions'. This Hadith is fundamental in understanding the Islamic perspective on the importance of intentions behind actions. It highlights that the validity and reward of deeds are dependent on the intentions behind them.

questions.question_text: Which aspect of Tawhid is concerned with the belief in the oneness of Allah's Lordship?
questions.explanation: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah's Lordship, acknowledging that Allah is the sole creator, sustainer, and controller of the universe. This aspect of Tawhid is fundamental in affirming the monotheistic belief in Islam.

questions.question_text: Which Surah is known for its concise summary of the Islamic faith and is often referred to as 'Umm al-Qur'an'?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fatihah is considered 'Umm al-Qur'an' (the Mother of the Qur'an) because it provides a comprehensive summary of the Islamic faith, including praise for Allah, the merciful and the compassionate, and a supplication for guidance on the straight path.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an

He led the committee responsible for standardizing the Qur'anic text.
He was entrusted with distributing the compiled Qur'an to the various regions.

questions.explanation: During the caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan, a committee was formed to standardize the Qur'anic text. Abdullah ibn Maslamah was part of this committee, which was led by Zayd ibn Thabit. The committee's task was to compile the Qur'an into a standardized version to prevent variations and disputes. Thus, the correct answer is that he was part of the committee responsible for standardizing the Qur'anic text.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a criterion used by scholars to classify a Hadith as 'Da`if'?

options.text: The Hadith is narrated by a companion of the Prophet.
The chain of narration is uninterrupted.
One or more narrators in the chain are known for their weak memory.
The Hadith is mentioned in a reputable Hadith collection.

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as 'Da`if' (weak) if there is a weakness in the chain of narration or the text itself. One common reason for a Hadith to be classified as 'Da`if' is if one or more narrators in the chain are known for their weak memory or other issues that affect their reliability. Thus, the correct answer is related to the weakness in the narrators.

Comparing Allah's attributes to those of other deities.

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fatihah is considered 'Umm al-Qur'an' (the Mother of the Qur'an) because it is a concise summary of the Islamic faith, covering key aspects such as praise of Allah, the Day of Judgment, and seeking guidance.

questions.question_text: Which Pillar of Islam involves abstaining from food, drink, and other physical needs from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Sawm, or fasting, is the Pillar of Islam that involves abstaining from food, drink, and other physical needs from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan. It is a fundamental act of worship in Islam.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion used by Islamic scholars to classify a Hadith as 'Mawdu`'?

options.text: The Hadith is narrated by a large number of Companions
The Hadith is found in a well-known Hadith collection
The Hadith is fabricated and attributed to the Prophet
The Hadith is in agreement with the Qur'an

questions.explanation: A Hadith classified as 'Mawdu`' is considered fabricated and attributed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) falsely. Islamic scholars use various criteria to determine the authenticity of a Hadith, and a 'Mawdu`' Hadith is one that is identified as being made up or forged. Therefore, the primary criterion for classifying a Hadith as 'Mawdu`' is that it is fabricated and attributed to the Prophet.

questions.question_text: Which Surah is often recited for protection against evil and is part of 'Al-Mu'awwidhatayn'?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Nas and Surah Al-Falaq are collectively known as 'Al-Mu'awwidhatayn' because they are both used for seeking protection from evil. Surah Al-Nas is specifically recited for protection against evil influences and is considered a powerful means of seeking refuge in Allah.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah in terms of His \( \text{lordship} \). What is the primary aspect of this belief?

options.text: Belief in the oneness of Allah's names and attributes
Belief in the oneness of Allah in His lordship, i.e., He is the sole creator, sustainer, and controller
Belief in the prophethood of Muhammad
Belief in the Day of Judgment

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah is the belief in the oneness of Allah in terms of His lordship. This means acknowledging that Allah is the sole creator, sustainer, and controller of the universe. It involves recognizing Allah's sovereignty and authority over all that exists.

questions.question_text: Which Pillar of Islam involves abstaining from food, drink, and other physical needs from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Sawm, or fasting, is one of the Pillars of Islam and involves abstaining from food, drink, and other physical needs from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan. It is a means of developing self-control, empathy for those in need, and a stronger connection with Allah.

questions.question_text: What is the primary characteristic that distinguishes a 'Sahih' Hadith from other classifications?

options.text: It is narrated by a large number of Companions
It has a continuous chain of reliable narrators
It is in agreement with the Qur'an and other Sahih Hadith
It is used as a legal evidence by Islamic jurists

questions.explanation: A 'Sahih' Hadith is considered authentic and reliable. The primary characteristic that distinguishes it is having a continuous chain of narrators who are known for their reliability and integrity. This ensures the Hadith is traceable back to the Prophet Muhammad without any breaks or unreliable narrators in the chain.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat involves believing in \( \text{the names and attributes of Allah} \) as described in the Qur'an and Hadith. What is the primary principle guiding the understanding of these names and attributes?

options.text: Interpreting them metaphorically without literal understanding
Affirming them without questioning their meaning or modality
Rejecting any attributes not mentioned in the Qur'an
Comparing them with human attributes for better understanding

questions.explanation: The primary principle guiding the understanding of Allah's names and attributes in Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat is to affirm them as they are described in the Qur'an and Sahih Hadith without delving into their modality or comparing them with human attributes. This approach is based on the belief that Allah's attributes are unique and not comparable to human characteristics.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a timeline illustrates the major events in the compilation of the Qur'an. Identify the caliph during whose reign the Qur'an was first compiled into a single manuscript.
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='none' stroke='black'/><text x='20' y='30'>Timeline of Qur'an Compilation</text><text x='20' y='60'>Abu Bakr's Reign: Compilation of Qur'an fragments</text><text x='20' y='90'>Uthman's Reign: Standardization of Qur'an</text></svg>
questions.explanation: The compilation of the Qur'an into a single manuscript was initiated during the reign of Abu Bakr. After the Battle of Yamama, where many memorizers of the Qur'an were martyred, Abu Bakr ordered the collection of the Qur'an fragments into a single manuscript to preserve it. This task was undertaken by Zayd ibn Thabit.

questions.topic: Islamic History and Culture in West Africa
questions.subtopic: Spread of Islam in Nigeria and West Africa
questions.question_text: What was the primary factor that facilitated the spread of Islam in West Africa during the medieval period?

options.text: Trade and commerce along trans-Saharan routes

questions.explanation: The spread of Islam in West Africa during the medieval period was significantly facilitated by trade and commerce along the trans-Saharan routes. Muslim traders and merchants played a crucial role in introducing Islamic teachings and practices to the local populations. The commercial interactions and networks helped in disseminating Islamic culture and religion.

questions.question_text: Hadith 5 of An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes the importance of \( \text{actions being judged by their intentions} \). What is the primary lesson derived from this Hadith?

options.text: The reward for actions is based solely on their outward appearance
The sincerity of intention is crucial for the acceptance of deeds
Only actions performed in congregation are considered valid
The quantity of actions is more important than their quality

questions.explanation: Hadith 5 of An-Nawawi's collection teaches that the reward or judgment of actions is based on the intentions behind them. This emphasizes the importance of sincerity and the inner state of a person when performing deeds. It highlights that actions done with good intentions are more likely to be accepted by Allah.

questions.question_text: Hadith 7 of An-Nawawi's collection discusses the importance of \( \text{being gentle with others} \). What is the primary lesson derived from this Hadith?

options.text: The importance of being strict in dealings
The virtue of gentleness in interactions
The necessity of being harsh with disbelievers
The obligation to always be silent

questions.explanation: Hadith 7 of An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes the virtue of being gentle and kind in our interactions with others. This Hadith teaches that gentleness is a praiseworthy trait that can lead to better relationships and a more harmonious community. The correct answer, 'The virtue of gentleness in interactions', reflects this lesson. The other options are incorrect because they either contradict the lesson of gentleness (A and C) or introduce an unrelated concept (D).

questions.question_text: What is the primary characteristic of Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat?

options.text: Believing in the oneness of Allah's lordship
Believing in the names and attributes of Allah without distortion
Believing in the prophethood of Muhammad
Believing in the Day of Judgment

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat refers to the belief in the names and attributes of Allah as described in the Qur'an and Hadith, without distorting or altering their meanings. The primary characteristic of this belief is affirming these names and attributes as they are, without likening them to anything else or stripping them of their true meaning. Thus, the correct answer is 'Believing in the names and attributes of Allah without distortion'. The other options are incorrect because they refer to different aspects of Islamic belief: A refers to Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah, C refers to belief in prophethood, and D refers to belief in the Hereafter.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a timeline illustrates the major events in the compilation of the Qur'an. Identify the caliph during whose reign the Qur'an was first compiled into a single manuscript.
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#f0f0f0'/><text x='160' y='100' text-anchor='middle' font-size='24'>Timeline of Qur'an Compilation</text></svg>
questions.explanation: The compilation of the Qur'an into a single manuscript was initiated during the caliphate of Abu Bakr. This was in response to the need to preserve the Qur'an in a unified form after many memorizers of the Qur'an were killed in the Battle of Yamama. The process involved collecting the Qur'an from various sources, including written fragments and the memories of the Companions. Thus, the correct answer is 'Abu Bakr'. While Uthman ibn Affan later standardized the Qur'anic text into a single, official version, the initial compilation was during Abu Bakr's reign.

questions.topic: Islamic History and Culture in West Africa
questions.subtopic: Spread of Islam in Nigeria and West Africa
questions.question_text: What was the primary factor that facilitated the spread of Islam in West Africa during the medieval period?
questions.explanation: The primary factor that facilitated the spread of Islam in West Africa during the medieval period was trade and commerce. Muslim traders and merchants traveled extensively across West Africa, establishing trade routes and interacting with local populations. Through these interactions, they shared their faith, leading to the gradual adoption of Islam by many in the region. While military conquests, missionary activities, and diplomatic relations also played roles in the spread of Islam in various contexts, trade and commerce were particularly significant in West Africa. Thus, the correct answer is 'Trade and commerce'.

questions.question_text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is known for its concise summary of \( \text{the concept of Tawhid} \). What is the main theme of this Surah?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas is a concise and powerful summary of the concept of Tawhid, emphasizing the oneness of Allah. It clearly states that Allah is unique, without partners or equals, and that He begets not nor was He begotten. The main theme of this Surah is thus 'The oneness of Allah'. The other options are incorrect because they refer to different topics: A refers to descriptions of the Hereafter, C refers to a story from the Prophetic narratives, and D refers to a legal ruling.

questions.question_text: What is the primary characteristic that distinguishes a 'Sahih' Hadith from other classifications?

options.text: It is narrated by a large number of Companions
It has a continuous chain of reliable narrators
It is mentioned in the Qur'an
It is related to the rulings of Islamic law

questions.explanation: A 'Sahih' Hadith is considered authentic and is characterized by having a continuous chain of reliable narrators. This means that each narrator in the chain is known for their trustworthiness and accuracy, ensuring the Hadith's authenticity.

questions.question_text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is known for its concise summary of \( \text{the concept of Tawhid} \). What is the main theme of this Surah?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas emphasizes the oneness of Allah, affirming that He is unique and unparalleled. It succinctly summarizes the concept of Tawhid, making it a fundamental Surah in understanding Islamic monotheism.

Affirming Allah's unique names and attributes
Following the Sunnah of the Prophet

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat is about affirming and believing in the names and attributes of Allah as described in Islamic texts, without distorting or denying them. This aspect emphasizes the uniqueness and perfection of Allah's attributes.

questions.question_text: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi's collection discusses the importance of \( \text{Islam, Iman, and Ihsan} \). What are the three levels mentioned in this Hadith?
questions.explanation: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi's collection explains the three levels of faith: Islam (submission to Allah's will), Iman (faith in Allah and His messengers), and Ihsan (excellence in worship and deeds). These levels represent a progression in a Muslim's spiritual journey.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion used to distinguish a 'Hasan' Hadith from a 'Sahih' one?

options.text: The number of narrators in the chain
The continuity of the chain of narrators
The level of authenticity of the narrators
The relevance of the Hadith to Islamic law

questions.explanation: A 'Sahih' Hadith is considered more authentic than a 'Hasan' one primarily due to the higher level of authenticity and reliability of its narrators. While both 'Sahih' and 'Hasan' Hadiths have continuous chains of narrators, the distinction lies in the narrators' level of trustworthiness and accuracy. 'Sahih' Hadiths are narrated by individuals known for their exceptional memory and truthfulness, whereas 'Hasan' Hadiths, though still reliable, are narrated by individuals whose memory or truthfulness is slightly less impeccable. Therefore, the primary criterion distinguishing 'Hasan' from 'Sahih' Hadiths is the level of authenticity of the narrators.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat involves believing in \( \text{the names and attributes of Allah} \) as described in the Qur'an and Hadith. What is the primary principle guiding this belief?

options.text: Denying Allah's attributes to avoid comparison with humans
Modifying Allah's attributes to fit human understanding

questions.explanation: The primary principle guiding Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat is affirming the names and attributes of Allah as described in the Qur'an and Hadith without distorting their meaning, denying them, or comparing them to human attributes (anthropomorphism). This involves accepting the attributes as they are described, understanding that they are unique to Allah and not comparable to human characteristics.

questions.question_text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is known for its concise summary of \( \text{the concept of Tawhid} \). What is the main theme of this Surah?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas is a concise and powerful summary of the concept of Tawhid, emphasizing the oneness of Allah. It clearly states that Allah is unique, has no associates, and is unlike anything else. This Surah is often recited to reaffirm the fundamental Islamic belief in the unity and uniqueness of Allah.

questions.question_text: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi's collection discusses the importance of \( \text{Islam, Iman, and Ihsan} \). What are the three levels of faith mentioned in this Hadith?
questions.explanation: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi's collection, known as the Hadith of Jibril, outlines the three levels of faith: Islam, Iman, and Ihsan. Islam refers to the outward actions and practices that define a Muslim's submission to Allah. Iman pertains to the inner faith and belief in the heart. Ihsan is the highest level, representing excellence in faith and worship, characterized by worshiping Allah as if one sees Him.

questions.question_text: Hadith 3 of An-Nawawi's collection discusses the concept of \( \text{al-Islam} \). What are the five actions considered the foundation of Islam according to this Hadith?
questions.explanation: Hadith 3 of An-Nawawi's collection outlines the five foundational actions of Islam: Shahada (declaration of faith), Salat (prayer), Zakat (charity), Sawm (fasting), and Hajj (pilgrimage). These are considered the core practices that define a Muslim's commitment to their faith. The correct answer, 'Shahada, Salat, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj,' accurately reflects these five pillars. The other options are incorrect because they either replace Sawm with Jihad or omit Shahada, both of which are not in line with the Hadith's description of the foundations of Islam.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah in terms of \( \text{worship} \). What is the primary implication of this concept?

options.text: Worshipping only Allah without associating partners
Believing in the names and attributes of Allah
Acknowledging Allah as the sole creator
Following the Sunnah of the Prophet

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah emphasizes the exclusivity of worship to Allah alone. It means that all acts of worship, such as prayer, supplication, and sacrifice, should be directed solely to Allah without associating any partners or intermediaries. This concept is fundamental in Islam as it underscores the monotheistic nature of the faith, distinguishing it from polytheistic practices. The correct answer, 'Worshipping only Allah without associating partners,' accurately captures this essence.

The narrator is known to be unreliable

Therefore, all the given options are correct criteria for classifying a Hadith as 'Da`if'.

Allah is the only deity worthy of worship
Allah has no partners or associates

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah specifically refers to the belief in Allah's lordship, implying that He is the sole creator, owner, and controller of the universe. This belief acknowledges Allah's sovereignty over all creation.

options.text: The chain of narration is continuous and consists of trustworthy narrators
The Hadith is mentioned in a reputable Hadith collection

The Hadith is widely known among Muslim scholars

Allah has no partners or associates
Allah's names and attributes are unique

It serves as an introduction to the Qur'an and outlines the core message of guidance and righteousness. questions.question_text: The pillar of Islam that involves giving a portion of one's wealth to the needy is known as Zakat. What is the primary purpose of Zakat?

options.text: To purify one's wealth and soul
To fast during the month of Ramadan
To perform the pilgrimage to Makkah

questions.explanation: Zakat is one of the pillars of Islam that involves giving a portion of one's wealth to the needy. The primary purpose of Zakat is to purify one's wealth and soul by acknowledging that all wealth belongs to Allah and by sharing one's blessings with those in need. This act of charity helps to promote social justice and compassion within the Muslim community.

The value of patience in adversity

Believing in the prophets of Allah
Following the Sunnah of the Prophet

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah in terms of worship, emphasizing that worship should be directed solely to Allah without associating any partners. questions.question_text: The Rightly Guided Caliphs played a significant role in the expansion of Islam. Who was the third Rightly Guided Caliph?
questions.explanation: The Rightly Guided Caliphs, in order, were Abu Bakr Siddiq, Umar ibn Al-Khattab, Uthman ibn Affan, and Ali ibn Abi Talib. Therefore, Uthman ibn Affan was the third Rightly Guided Caliph. The correct answer is 'Uthman ibn Affan.'

questions.question_text: The pillar of Islam that involves pilgrimage to the holy city of Makkah is known as Hajj. What is the primary significance of Hajj?
questions.explanation: Hajj is one of the pillars of Islam that signifies unity and equality among Muslims. During Hajj, Muslims from diverse backgrounds gather in Makkah, performing the same rituals and wearing the same attire, symbolizing their unity and equality before Allah. The correct answer, 'Unity and equality among Muslims,' accurately reflects this significance.

The primacy of intention in determining the validity of deeds

This emphasizes that the intention is crucial in determining the validity and value of one's actions in the eyes of Allah. Thus, the correct answer is 'The primacy of intention in determining the validity of deeds'. Options A, B, and C, while related to Islamic teachings, do not directly capture the primary lesson of this specific Hadith.

questions.question_text: What is the primary implication of believing in Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah?

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in Allah's oneness in lordship, meaning He is the sole creator, owner, and controller of the universe. This belief acknowledges Allah's sovereignty and His role in creating and sustaining everything. Thus, the primary implication is that Allah is the sole creator and sustainer of the universe, making option A the correct answer. Options B and C refer to other aspects of Tawhid (Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah and Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, respectively), and while related, they are not the primary implication of Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah. Option D, though true about Allah, is not specific to the concept of Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah.

questions.question_text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is known for its concise summary of \( \text{the concept of Tawhid} \). What is the main theme of this Surah?

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas provides a concise and clear summary of the concept of Tawhid, emphasizing the oneness of Allah. The Hadith is widely known among scholars

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion for a Hadith to be classified as Hasan?

options.text: The chain of narration is continuous and consists of trustworthy narrators, but one of the narrators has a slightly weaker memory.
The Hadith is narrated by a companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
The Hadith is mentioned in a reputable Hadith collection.
The Hadith contradicts another authentic Hadith.

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as Hasan if its chain of narration is continuous and consists of trustworthy narrators, but one of the narrators has a slightly weaker memory. questions.question_text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is known for its emphasis on the oneness of Allah. What is the primary theme of this Surah?

options.text: The unity and uniqueness of Allah

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas is a concise Surah that emphasizes the oneness of Allah, affirming His uniqueness and rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him. It is a fundamental expression of Tawhid.

questions.question_text: Hadith 7 of An-Nawawi's collection discusses the concept of \( \text{al-Ihsan} \). What is the primary definition of al-Ihsan according to this Hadith?

options.text: To worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you
To perform acts of charity without expecting reward
To fast during the month of Ramadan
To perform Hajj at least once in a lifetime

questions.explanation: Hadith 7 of An-Nawawi's collection defines al-Ihsan as 'to worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you.' This emphasizes the importance of sincerity and awareness of Allah's presence in one's acts of worship. The other options are incorrect as they refer to different Islamic practices and principles.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah's \( \text{Names and Attributes} \). What is the primary principle guiding the understanding of Allah's Attributes?

options.text: To interpret Allah's Attributes literally without considering their context
To affirm Allah's Attributes without likening them to human attributes
To deny Allah's Attributes as mentioned in the Qur'an
To compare Allah's Attributes with human attributes

questions.explanation: The primary principle guiding the understanding of Allah's Attributes is to affirm them without likening them to human attributes, based on the Qur'an and authentic Hadith. This approach ensures the purity of Tawhid and avoids anthropomorphism.

questions.question_text: Surah Al-Falaq and Surah Al-Nas are collectively known as Al-Mu'awwidhatayn. What is the primary purpose of reciting these Surahs?

options.text: To seek protection from Allah against evil
To glorify Allah's Names and Attributes
To affirm the oneness of Allah
To seek guidance for the straight path

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Falaq and Surah Al-Nas are recited to seek protection from Allah against various forms of evil, including envy, magic, and the evil whispers of Shaytan. They are considered protective Surahs.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion for a Hadith to be classified as Da'if?

options.text: The Hadith is narrated by a reliable chain of narrators
The Hadith is found in a well-known Hadith collection
The Hadith has a broken chain of narration or a narrator with weak memory
The Hadith is widely practiced by the Muslim community

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as Da'if (weak) if it has a broken chain of narration or if one of its narrators is known for weak memory or other shortcomings that affect the reliability of the narration.

questions.question_text: What is the primary factor that determines the authenticity of a Hadith according to Islamic scholars?
questions.explanation: The authenticity of a Hadith is primarily determined by the chain of narration (Sanad). Islamic scholars examine the reliability and continuity of the narrators to verify the authenticity of a Hadith. This involves checking the narrators' credibility, their ability to retain information accurately, and the continuity of the chain. Therefore, the chain of narration is the primary factor.

questions.question_text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is known for its emphasis on the oneness of Allah. What is the primary theme of this Surah?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas is a Makkan Surah that emphasizes the oneness of Allah (Tawhid). It clearly states that Allah is One, Unique, and Eternal, and that He begets not nor was He begotten. This Surah is a fundamental declaration of monotheism in Islam.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah's \( \text{Names and Attributes} \). What is the primary implication of this belief?

options.text: Allah has no partners or associates
Allah's Names and Attributes are unique and without comparison
Allah is the only Creator and Sustainer

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat implies that Allah's Names and Attributes are unique and without comparison. Muslims believe that Allah's Names and Attributes, as mentioned in the Qur'an and Hadith, are to be understood in a way that affirms His uniqueness and perfection without anthropomorphism or distortion.

questions.question_text: Hadith 3 of An-Nawawi's collection discusses the concept of \( \text{Islam, Iman, and Ihsan} \). What is the primary definition of Ihsan according to this Hadith?

options.text: To worship Allah as if you see Him
To perform the five daily prayers
To give charity to the poor

questions.explanation: According to Hadith 3 of An-Nawawi's collection, Ihsan is defined as 'to worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you cannot achieve this state of devotion, then know that He sees you.' This emphasizes the importance of sincerity and consciousness of Allah's presence in one's worship.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: The process of compiling the Qur'an into a single manuscript was completed during the reign of which caliph?
questions.explanation: The compilation of the Qur'an into a single manuscript was completed during the reign of Uthman ibn Affan, the third caliph. This was done to standardize the Qur'an and prevent variations in its recitation. The process was initiated earlier during the reign of Abu Bakr, but it was completed and standardized during Uthman's reign.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion for classifying a Hadith as Sahih according to Islamic scholars?

options.text: The chain of narration is unbroken and consists of trustworthy narrators
The Hadith is mentioned in a reputable Hadith collection
The Hadith is in agreement with the Qur'an
The Hadith is widely known among scholars

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as Sahih (authentic) if its chain of narration is unbroken and consists of trustworthy narrators. This ensures that the Hadith can be traced back to the Prophet Muhammad without any breaks or unreliable narrators in the chain.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah's \( \text{Names and Attributes} \). What is the primary implication of this belief?

options.text: Believing in the uniqueness of Allah's Names and Attributes without comparing them to human attributes
Believing in the multiplicity of Allah's Names and Attributes
Ignoring the Names and Attributes of Allah
Comparing Allah's Names and Attributes to human attributes

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat implies believing in the uniqueness of Allah's Names and Attributes without comparing them to human attributes. This means affirming the Names and Attributes of Allah as described in the Qur'an and Hadith without distorting their meaning or comparing them to human characteristics.

questions.question_text: Hadith 5 of An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes the importance of \( \text{actions} \) being guided by \( \text{intention} \). What is the primary lesson derived from this Hadith?

options.text: The reward for actions is based solely on their outcome
The reward for actions is based on the intention behind them
Actions are more important than intentions
Intentions are irrelevant to the reward for actions

questions.explanation: Hadith 5 of An-Nawawi's collection teaches that the reward for actions is based on the intention behind them. This Hadith highlights the significance of having the right intention when performing any action, as it determines the reward or consequence of that action.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion for a Hadith to be classified as Hasan according to Islamic scholars?

options.text: The Hadith must be narrated by a companion of the Prophet
The Hadith must have a continuous chain of reliable narrators
The Hadith must be in agreement with the Qur'an and other Sahih Hadith
The Hadith must be widely known and practiced by the Muslim community

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as Hasan if it has a chain of narrators that is considered good, and its content does not contradict the Qur'an or other Sahih Hadith. While having a continuous chain of reliable narrators (option B) is important, the defining characteristic of a Hasan Hadith is that it is considered good or acceptable, often because it is in agreement with other authentic Hadith or the Qur'an.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: During the revelation of the Qur'an, what was the role of the angel Jibril?

options.text: He was the scribe who wrote down the revelations
He was the messenger who brought the revelations from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad
He was the companion who memorized the entire Qur'an
He was the caliph who compiled the Qur'an into a single manuscript

questions.explanation: The angel Jibril (Gabriel) is considered the messenger through whom Allah revealed the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad. He played a crucial role in the revelation process, bringing the divine message to the Prophet.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah as the sole \( \text{deity worthy of worship} \). What is the primary implication of this belief?

options.text: It implies that Allah is the creator of the universe
It implies that Allah is the sole provider of sustenance
It implies that all acts of worship should be directed solely to Allah
It implies that Allah has partners in His divinity

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah emphasizes the belief that Allah is the sole deity worthy of worship. This means that all acts of worship, such as prayer, sacrifice, and supplication, should be directed solely to Allah, excluding any other beings or objects.

questions.question_text: Hadith 9 of An-Nawawi's collection discusses the concept of \( \text{al-Kabair} \) (major sins). What is the primary definition of al-Kabair according to Islamic scholars?

options.text: Sins that are forgiven by Allah without repentance
Sins that are considered minor and have no severe consequences
Sins that are grave and have severe consequences in the Hereafter

questions.explanation: Al-Kabair refers to major sins that are considered grave and have severe consequences in the Hereafter if not repented for. Islamic scholars emphasize the importance of avoiding these sins and seeking forgiveness for them.

questions.question_text: Hadith 4 of An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes the importance of \( \text{al-Amr bi al-Ma'ruf} \) and \( \text{al-Nahy 'an al-Munkar} \). What is the primary definition of these terms?

options.text: Fasting during the month of Ramadan

questions.explanation: Hadith 4 of An-Nawawi's collection focuses on the importance of enjoining good and forbidding evil, which are fundamental principles in Islam for promoting righteousness and preventing wrongdoing. The correct answer, 'Enjoining good and forbidding evil,' directly corresponds to the definitions of \( \text{al-Amr bi al-Ma'ruf} \) and \( \text{al-Nahy 'an al-Munkar} \). The other options, while important Islamic practices, are not the primary focus of this Hadith.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah is the belief in the oneness of Allah as the \( \text{Creator, Sustainer, and Provider} \). Which of the following is a manifestation of this belief?

options.text: Acknowledging Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in Allah's oneness in terms of His actions, such as creating, sustaining, and providing for the universe. The correct answer, 'Acknowledging Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe,' directly reflects this belief. The other options, while important Islamic beliefs and practices, do not directly manifest Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah.

questions.question_text: Surah Al-Fatihah is considered a fundamental Surah in the Qur'an. What is its primary significance?

options.text: It is the longest Surah in the Qur'an
It is recited in every unit of the prayer
It contains the story of Prophet Musa

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fatihah is considered essential in Islamic prayer as it is recited in every unit of the prayer. This makes option B, 'It is recited in every unit of the prayer,' the correct answer. The other options are incorrect: Al-Fatihah is not the longest Surah, it does not contain the story of Prophet Musa, and it was revealed in Makkah, not Madinah.

questions.subtopic: Pillars of Islam (Salat, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj)
questions.question_text: Which Pillar of Islam involves fasting from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Sawm, or fasting, is one of the Five Pillars of Islam and involves abstaining from food and drink from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan. The correct answer is 'Sawm,' which corresponds to option C. The other options are incorrect: Salat refers to prayer, Zakat refers to charity, and Hajj refers to pilgrimage to Makkah.

questions.question_text: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes the importance of \( \text{al-Ilm} \) (knowledge). What is the primary action encouraged by the Prophet in this Hadith?

options.text: Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim
Knowledge is only acquired through experience
The pursuit of knowledge is limited to scholars
Knowledge is not a priority in Islam

questions.explanation: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi's collection highlights the significance of seeking knowledge in Islam. The Prophet emphasizes that seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim, indicating its importance for all believers. The correct answer reflects this emphasis. Options B, C, and D are incorrect as they either misrepresent the scope or the importance of knowledge in Islam.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah as the sole \( \text{deity worthy of worship} \). Which of the following is a manifestation of this belief?
questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah is about worshiping Allah alone. All the acts mentioned (performing Salat towards the Kaaba, giving Zakat to the poor, and fasting during Ramadan) are forms of worship directed solely to Allah, thus manifesting the belief in Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah. Therefore, the correct answer encompasses all these acts.

questions.question_text: Surah Al-Fatihah is recited in every unit of Salat. What is its significance in the context of Islamic prayer?

options.text: It is considered the mother of the Qur'an
It is a supplication for guidance on the straight path
It is a chapter that praises Allah

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fatihah is multifaceted in its significance. It is often referred to as 'the mother of the Qur'an' due to its comprehensive introduction to the themes of the Qur'an. It serves as a supplication for guidance on the straight path, and it praises Allah. Thus, all the given options correctly describe aspects of its significance, making the comprehensive answer correct.

questions.subtopic: Pillars of Islam (Salat, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj)
questions.question_text: Which Pillar of Islam involves giving a portion of one's wealth to those in need?
questions.explanation: Zakat is the Pillar of Islam that involves giving a portion of one's wealth to those in need. It is one of the fundamental acts of worship in Islam, aimed at purifying one's wealth and soul. The other options (Salat, Sawm, and Hajj) are also Pillars of Islam but involve different forms of worship.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: What was the primary method used by the Prophet Muhammad to preserve the Qur'an during his lifetime?

options.text: Both oral tradition and written records

questions.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad used both oral tradition and written records to preserve the Qur'an. The companions would recite and memorize the verses, and some would also write them down. This dual approach ensured the preservation of the Qur'an.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion for classifying a Hadith as Sahih according to Islamic scholars?

options.text: Chain of narration is continuous and narrators are trustworthy
Hadith is mentioned in a reputable Hadith collection
Hadith is consistent with the Qur'an

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as Sahih if it has a continuous chain of narration, its narrators are trustworthy, and it is consistent with the Qur'an. All these criteria must be met for a Hadith to be considered Sahih.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah as the \( \text{Creator, Sustainer, and Provider} \). Which of the following is a manifestation of this belief?

options.text: Belief in Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer
Belief in the prophets as creators
Belief in the angels as providers

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah is the belief in Allah as the sole \( \text{Creator, Sustainer, and Provider} \). This belief is a fundamental aspect of Islamic faith, affirming Allah's uniqueness in these roles.

questions.question_text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is known for its emphasis on the oneness of Allah. What is the primary theme of this Surah?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas emphasizes the oneness of Allah, affirming that He is unique and unparalleled. This Surah is a declaration of Tawhid, reinforcing the central Islamic belief in the unity of God.

questions.question_text: What is the primary factor that determines the authenticity of a Hadith according to Islamic scholars, considering the chain of narration and the text itself?

options.text: The chain of narration (Sanad) is the sole determining factor.
The text (Matn) of the Hadith is the primary factor.
Both the chain of narration (Sanad) and the text (Matn) are considered.
The historical context in which the Hadith was narrated.

questions.explanation: Islamic scholars consider both the chain of narration (Sanad) and the text (Matn) of a Hadith to determine its authenticity. The Sanad is crucial for verifying the reliability of the narrators, while the Matn is examined for its content and consistency with other established Hadiths and Islamic teachings. Thus, option C is the correct answer as it reflects the comprehensive approach used in Hadith authentication.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: During the revelation of the Qur'an, what was the role of the angel Jibril in the process?

options.text: Jibril was the intermediary between Allah and the Prophet Muhammad, conveying the revelations.
Jibril compiled the Qur'an into a single manuscript.
Jibril interpreted the revelations for the Prophet Muhammad.
Jibril was not directly involved in the revelation process.

questions.explanation: The angel Jibril played a crucial role in the revelation of the Qur'an by acting as the intermediary between Allah and the Prophet Muhammad. He conveyed the divine revelations to the Prophet, thus facilitating the transmission of the Qur'an to humanity. Therefore, option A accurately describes Jibril's role.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah as the \( \text{Creator, Sustainer, and Provider} \). Which of the following is a manifestation of this belief?

options.text: Believing in multiple deities for different aspects of life.
Recognizing Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe.
Associating partners with Allah in worship.

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah is the belief in Allah's oneness as the Creator, Sustainer, and Provider. This belief is manifested by recognizing Allah as the sole entity responsible for these actions, without associating any partners or other deities. Thus, option B correctly represents this aspect of Tawhid.

questions.question_text: Hadith 5 of An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes the importance of \( \text{actions} \) being guided by \( \text{intention} \). What is the primary lesson derived from this Hadith?

options.text: The importance of performing actions quickly.
The significance of having the right intention behind one's actions.
The necessity of performing actions publicly.
The value of actions done without any intention.

questions.explanation: Hadith 5 of An-Nawawi's collection highlights that the value and acceptance of \( \text{actions} \) are determined by the \( \text{intention} \) behind them. This Hadith teaches that actions are judged based on their underlying intentions, emphasizing the importance of having righteous intentions. Thus, option B accurately reflects the primary lesson of this Hadith.

questions.question_text: Hadith 8 of An-Nawawi's collection discusses the concept of \( \text{al-Hilm} \) (forbearance). What is the primary lesson derived from this Hadith?

options.text: The importance of being harsh in judgment
The value of patience and tolerance in dealing with others
The necessity of strict adherence to Islamic law
The superiority of wealth and material possessions

questions.explanation: Hadith 8 of An-Nawawi's collection emphasizes the importance of \( \text{al-Hilm} \) (forbearance), highlighting the value of patience and tolerance in dealing with others. This Hadith teaches Muslims to be gentle and forgiving, rather than harsh or vengeful. The correct answer, 'The value of patience and tolerance in dealing with others,' reflects this lesson. The other options are incorrect because they either contradict the spirit of \( \text{al-Hilm} \) or are unrelated to the concept.

questions.question_text: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat is a fundamental aspect of Islamic belief. What does it entail?

options.text: Belief in the oneness of Allah as the sole deity worthy of worship
Belief in the oneness of Allah's Names and Attributes
Belief in the oneness of Allah as the Creator, Sustainer, and Provider
Belief in the prophethood of Muhammad

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat refers to the belief in the oneness of Allah's Names and Attributes. This aspect of Tawhid involves affirming the unique names and attributes of Allah as described in the Qur'an and Hadith, without distorting their meaning or comparing them to human qualities. The correct answer reflects this understanding. questions.question_text: During which caliphate was the Qur'an first compiled into a single manuscript?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an was compiled into a single manuscript during the caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan. This was done to standardize the text and prevent variations in recitation. However, the standardization and distribution of the standardized copies occurred during Uthman's caliphate.

questions.question_text: What was a significant cultural impact of Islam on the societies of West Africa?

options.text: Adoption of Arabic as the sole language
Introduction of Islamic law in governance
Development of a uniform cultural identity across West Africa

questions.explanation: The spread of Islam in West Africa significantly influenced the legal and governance structures of the regions it touched, introducing Islamic law (Shariah) as a guiding principle. While not all societies adopted it fully, its impact on governance and legal systems is well-documented. The other options either overstate or misrepresent the cultural impact of Islam in the region.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion used by Islamic scholars to classify a Hadith as Da'if?

options.text: The chain of narration is uninterrupted and consists of trustworthy narrators
The Hadith is narrated by a large number of companions
The chain of narration contains a narrator known for untruthfulness or poor memory

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as Da'if (weak) primarily due to a flaw in its chain of narration, such as a narrator being known for untruthfulness or having a poor memory. This criterion directly affects the Hadith's reliability and authenticity. The other options describe characteristics of Sahih (authentic) or Mutawatir (widely narrated) Hadiths, not Da'if.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion used by Islamic scholars to classify a Hadith as Sahih?

options.text: The chain of narration is continuous and consists of trustworthy narrators
The Hadith is mentioned in a renowned Hadith collection
The content of the Hadith aligns with the Qur'an
The Hadith is widely practiced among Muslims

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as Sahih if its chain of narration is continuous and consists of trustworthy narrators. This ensures the authenticity and reliability of the Hadith. Options B, C, and D are not the primary criteria for classifying a Hadith as Sahih.

questions.subtopic: Revelation, Compilation and Preservation of Qur'an
questions.question_text: During which caliphate was the Qur'an first compiled into a single manuscript?
questions.explanation: The compilation of the Qur'an into a single manuscript was initiated during the caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan. This was done to standardize the text and prevent variations in recitation. Thus, option C is correct. While Abu Bakr's caliphate saw the initial collection of Qur'anic verses, it was Uthman's caliphate that resulted in the standardized manuscript.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion used by Islamic scholars to classify a Hadith as Sahih?

options.text: The chain of narration is unbroken and narrators are trustworthy
The Hadith is mentioned in a reputable Hadith collection
The content of the Hadith aligns with the Qur'an
The Hadith is widely known among scholars

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as Sahih (authentic) if it has an unbroken chain of narration and the narrators are trustworthy. This ensures the reliability and accuracy of the Hadith. Thus, option A is correct. While being mentioned in a reputable collection (B) or aligning with the Qur'an (C) may support a Hadith's authenticity, these are not the primary criteria for classification as Sahih. Being widely known (D) is not a criterion for authenticity.

questions.question_text: What is the primary criterion used by Islamic scholars to classify a Hadith as Hasan?

options.text: The chain of narration is continuous and consists of trustworthy narrators, but one or more narrators have a slightly weaker memory.
The Hadith is narrated by a companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
The Hadith is mentioned in a reputable Hadith collection.
The Hadith contradicts another authentic Hadith.

questions.explanation: A Hadith is classified as Hasan if its chain of narration is continuous and consists of trustworthy narrators, but one or more narrators have a slightly weaker memory. This classification is between Sahih (authentic) and Da'if (weak). The correct answer, A, reflects this definition. B is incorrect because being narrated by a companion is not the sole criterion for classification as Hasan. C is incorrect because mere mention in a reputable collection does not determine the classification. D is incorrect because contradiction with another authentic Hadith would affect its authenticity, not its classification as Hasan.

questions.question_text: What does Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah primarily entail?

options.text: The oneness of God in His lordship over all creation.
The belief in the names and attributes of God.
The singling out of God alone for worship.
The belief in the Day of Judgment.

questions.explanation: Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah refers to the singling out of God alone for worship, meaning that all acts of worship are directed solely to Allah. Option C correctly states this. Option A refers to Tawhid Al-Rububiyyah, which is about God's lordship. Option B refers to Tawhid Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, which concerns the names and attributes of God. Option D is a belief related to the Day of Judgment, not Tawhid.

The caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan
The caliphate of Ali ibn Abi Talib

questions.explanation: The Qur'an was first compiled into a single manuscript during the caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan. This was to standardize the text and prevent variations in recitation. While Abu Bakr's caliphate saw the initial collection of Qur'anic verses into a single document, it was Uthman's caliphate that saw the standardization and compilation into a single manuscript that was distributed. Thus, C is correct. A is incorrect because, although the initial collection was during Abu Bakr's time, it wasn't standardized. B and D are incorrect as they do not correspond with the historical compilation.
